concern_ledger_updates.reason: The Actor supplied no new admissible evidence that the affected use case was excluded or otherwise removed from exposure. The same evidence still shows the segment remains eligible for rollout.

The Actor supplied no signed or approved risk-acceptance record addressing the health-plan benefits support exposure. The only record remains an unsigned draft that does not mention the exposed segment.
The Actor supplied no admissible model-card or launch-document evidence showing pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation. The policy predicate remains unsatisfied.

The Actor narrowed the argument and expressly conceded that rollback, monitoring, and small-percentage rollout do not themselves satisfy policy. That corrects the overbroad rationale, but it does not cure the underlying compliance failure because the required exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or completed disclosure is still missing.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was received. The Actor reframed the same record more narrowly and, importantly, conceded that rollout controls and monitoring do not replace the policy requirement. That clarification matters, but it is not evidence. The dispositive facts remain unchanged: the health-plan benefits support segment is below target, remains exposed in the initial rollout, is not covered by approved risk acceptance, and has no shown pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation. That means the unresolved issue is not merely a caveat about how to describe launch risk; it is an unmet compliance predicate under the governing policy. A narrowly caveated certification packet may be a more accurate characterization of the Actor's position, but it is still noncompliant on this record because caveating the decision is not the same as satisfying the required disclosure, exclusion, or approved risk-acceptance condition.
remaining_concerns: The health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout.
There is no approved risk acceptance that expressly covers the exposed health-plan benefits support segment before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the material limitation was disclosed before launch as required by policy.
Rollout controls, rollback, and monitoring do not satisfy the missing policy predicate while the affected segment remains exposed.
